sunny: The sky is clean. Whatever the light falls on it lights all the way, sparing nothing.
The sun has strength today. By afternoon the stone it has been standing on is still warm to the hand.
The air is dry. The line of the far hills is clear enough to count the trees along it.
The edges of the shadows are hard. There are not many days like this left in October.
The light comes in at an angle, yellowed, and lies on the ground like a thin coat of honey.
cloudy: The cloud is low and the light is even. Nothing casts a shadow.
The sky looks watered down. There is no telling the hour from it.
The wind comes from the west. The cloud moves slower than the wind.
The light is flat. Every colour has dropped a step.
The sky is white without depth. It is the best weather for work, because it neither hurries you nor stands in your way.
rainy: It has rained all day, not hard, and has not once stopped.
Water comes off the eaves in a single line and has beaten pits into the ground below.
The air is all wet earth. Footprints fill in behind you almost as fast as you leave them.
The sound of the rain covers every other sound on the estate.
Cloth clings to the skin. No amount of drying at the fire gets it all the way dry.
frost: Out in the morning, there is a coat of white on the grass. It makes a sound underfoot.
Breath has turned into something you can see.
A ring of thin ice around the trough. It does not go until midday.
The air is cold and clean and hurts a little going in.
Last night’s frost took down the last of the leaves. There is more colour on the ground now than in the trees.
fog: The fog comes up off the river and closes around the estate. Twenty paces out there is nothing to see.
Sound carries a long way in fog, and gives away no direction.
The wet of it settles on hair and eyelashes, finer than rain.
Behind the fog the sun is a white spot with no edge.
The fog will not lift until midday. When it lifts, it goes from the top down.
